chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the two judges to separate them until they consult the man and the woman and stipulate upon them both: "If we so desire, we will gather you together, and if we so desire, we will separate you both."'
So if they gather them both, it is valid/permissible; and if they separate them both, it is valid/permissible.

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: His family (referring to the husband's family)
key_terms.أَهْلِهَا: Her family (referring to the wife's family)
key_terms.حَكَمٌ: Judge or arbitrator appointed to resolve disputes

ai.seo_question: What is the role and authority of the two judges in resolving marital disputes according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the two judges are granted the authority to effect either reconciliation or separation, contingent upon the couple's prior consent to their verdict. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the judges' role is not merely advisory but executive, provided the spouses agree to be bound by their decision. The condition 'if we wish, we unite; if we wish, we separate' underscores the discretionary power of the judges to determine the outcome based on the specific circumstances of the discord.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:35] then appoint a judge from his family and a judge from her family.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for the two judges that they separate them until the man and the woman instruct them and they (two judges) stipulate upon them both, ‘If we so desire to we would get you two together, and if we so desire to we would separate you both’.
So if they gather them both, it is allowed, and if they separate them both, it is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘If you are afraid of discord between them then send one arbitrators from his people and another from her people.’ [4:35]

He (the Imam) said, ‘The arbitrator cannot separate or unite them without first getting approval from the man and woman and a stipulation that their decision of separating or uniting them must be treated binding.
Thus, if they decided for separation or unification it is permissible.’”
